content: Arvid Afzelius was a Swedish dermatologist who lived from 1857 to 1923. During his time as a student at the Karolinska Institutet, he studied under the renowned dermatologist Moritz Kaposi in Vienna. Kaposi is now widely recognized for the sarcoma named after him, which is a common lesion associated with acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS). In 1909, at a meeting of the Swedish Society of Dermatology, Afzelius presented his findings on an expanding, ring-shaped skin lesion he had observed. Twelve years later, he published his research and hypothesized that the rash was caused by the bite of an Ixodes tick. This rash, now known as Erythema migrans, represents the early stage of Borreliosis and is an initial clinical sign of Lyme disease. In recognition of his contributions, one of the Borrelia species responsible for Lyme disease, Borrelia afzelii, was named in his honor.
